info.title: Lenipo API
info.description: REST API of Lenipo. Browsers authenticate with the session cookie; scripts, the CLI and MCP clients with a personal access token (`Authorization: Bearer tl_pat_…`).

get.summary: Show version, runtime and database information
get.description: Requires the global permission `admin`.

get.summary: Sign-in rules: session lifetimes and groups that must use two-factor sign-in
get.description: Requires the global permission `admin`.

put.summary: Change the sign-in rules (TL-18)
put.description: Requires the global permission `admin`.

delete.summary: End every session of a user
Remove a user’s two-factor sign-in, e.g. after a lost phone
delete.description:
If a group demands it, the person sets it up again at the next sign-in.

Requires the global permission `admin`.

post.summary: Deactivate a user
post.description:
Ends their sessions, tokens and app connections; everything they did stays.

Requires the global permission `admin`.

post.summary: Make a user an external collaborator, or a regular one again
post.description:
External collaborators leave the group "users", hold no global permissions and only see the projects and spaces they are given (TL-66).

Requires the global permission `admin`.

post.summary: Reactivate a deactivated user
post.description: Requires the global permission `admin`.

post.summary: Anonymise a user (GDPR)
post.description:
Irreversible: name and e-mail become "Ehemalige Person n" everywhere, sign-in data and personal settings are deleted, contributions stay.

Requires the global permission `admin`.

Options are given as the full list; entries with an id are renamed or archived, entries without one are added, missing ones are archived.

get.summary: List the AI agents
get.description:
With vendor, model and responsible person; the web app marks them by this list.

Requires the global permission `browse-users`.

post.summary: Create an AI agent
post.description:
A user of the kind "agent" without password or sign-in. It joins only the groups named, not "users"; give it projects through their roles.

Requires the global permission `admin`.

patch.summary: Change an AI agent

get.summary: List the tokens of an AI agent
get.description: For its responsible person and administrators.

post.summary: Create a token for an AI agent; the secret is returned only once
post.description: Needs a browser session of its responsible person or an administrator. Agent tokens never carry the `admin` scope.

delete.summary: Revoke a token of an AI agent

put.summary: Pause an AI agent (Not-Aus)
put.description: For its responsible person and administrators. The agent then only reads: writing answers 423 with the reason, its claims end, its webhook rests and it takes no new work. Its tokens stay valid.

delete.summary: Let a paused AI agent work again

put.summary: Set the budget of an AI agent
put.description: Limits per day and month (UTC) for newly claimed issues, minutes holding claims and reported cost; null means none. The responsible person hears at 80 % and 100 %; while a limit is reached, new claims answer 409.

get.summary: Get the agent settings of a project
get.description: Whether agents need approval to start and complete sprints, and the roles of agents in the project. An agent without roles counts as implementer.

put.summary: Change the agent settings of a project
put.description: Approval for sprints, the statuses agents do not set themselves (a person approves the transition) and where reviews move the issue. Requires the project permission `administer`.

put.summary: Set the roles of an agent in the project
put.description: planner: plan, fill and start sprints; coordinator: complete them; implementer and tester: claim work; reviewer: review. No roles: implementer. Requires `administer`.

put.summary: Pause all agents in the project (Not-Aus)
put.description: They then only read here: writing answers 423 with the reason and their claims in the project end. Requires `administer`.

delete.summary: Let the agents of the project work again

put.summary: Set the webhook of an AI agent; the secret is returned only once
put.description: Every new notification of the agent (mentions, assignments, comments …) is sent there as `notification.created`, signed like all webhooks (Standard Webhooks) and retried. Setting it again replaces URL and secret. For its responsible person and administrators, in the browser.

delete.summary: Remove the webhook of an AI agent

get.summary: Get the active claim on an issue

post.summary: Claim an issue
post.description: Atomic: makes the caller the assignee of an unassigned issue and holds it for 30 minutes; every heartbeat (`PUT /me/presence`) extends the claims. 409 when someone else is assigned or works on it, and with `claimConflicts` when branch or paths overlap with other claims in the project, unless `force` is set. Claiming again renews and changes the work area.

delete.summary: Release a claim
delete.description: One’s own, or any as project administrator. The assignee stays.

get.summary: List the active claims of a project

post.summary: Claim the next fitting issue of a project
post.description: One’s own open claim first; otherwise unresolved issues of active and planned sprints, then of the whole project, in rank order, that are unassigned or one’s own, not claimed by others, not blocked by an unresolved issue and within the agent’s task filter and the optional `filter`. `claim` is null when nothing fits.

post.summary: Hand an issue over
post.description: Writes one comment marked as handover with what is done, what is open and notes. With `to` (id or e-mail) that person or agent becomes assignee, is mentioned and takes over the caller’s claim with its work area; without, the caller’s claim ends.

post.summary: Report a blocker
post.description: Links `blockedBy` as blocking issue, writes the note as comment and sets the caller’s heartbeat to blocked on this issue.

post.summary: Ask for a review of an issue’s work
post.description: Without `reviewer` Lenipo picks a reviewer agent of the project (role reviewer), never the requester or assignee, another vendor first, then the least busy. The reviewer is notified and finds the pull request in the answer.

get.summary: List the reviews of an issue
List the reviews the caller is asked for
get.description: Waiting ones by default, oldest first.

post.summary: Give the verdict of a review
post.description: Writes a review comment on the issue, tells the requester and moves the issue to the status the project set for this verdict, if any. Post in the pull request yourself; Lenipo does not write to the git host.

delete.summary: Withdraw a waiting review request

get.summary: List the transition approval requests of an issue

post.summary: Approve or reject a transition an agent asked for
post.description: For people who may move issues in the project. Approving moves the issue in the agent’s name; rejecting needs a reason, which the agent is told.

get.summary: List what waits for the caller’s approval
get.description: Sprint starts and completions (where the caller has `edit-issues`) and transitions (with `transition-issues`) agents asked for.

get.summary: The agents dashboard
get.description:
Every agent with its state and issue, budget use, issues resolved and failures (rejected writes, reviews with changes requested) in the last 7 days, and what it waits for.

Requires the global permission `browse-users`.

get.summary: Get the budget use of an AI agent
get.description: For the agent, its responsible person and administrators.

get.summary: Get the history of an AI agent
get.description: Its writing and rejected requests (kept 90 days), changes, comments, reviews and approval requests, newest first; changes and comments only on issues the caller can see.

get.summary: Get what an AI agent may do
get.description: Its groups, the projects it sees with permissions and roles, and its live tokens.

get.summary: Get the caller’s own budget use
get.description: For agents: what counts against their budget today and this month.

post.summary: Report the cost of a run
post.description: Agents report what a run cost, in the currency of their budget; Lenipo counts claims and claimed time itself.

put.summary: Send a heartbeat: state and what one is working on
put.description: Mainly for agents, e.g. at the start and end of each run. Without a new heartbeat for 30 minutes the state counts as offline. `issueKey` and `branch` stay as they are when left out; null clears them.

get.summary: Get the own state from the last heartbeat
Who works in the project
get.description: People and agents who changed something in the project in the last 30 days, have open issues there or a fresh heartbeat on one of its issues; with state, current issue and branch, last activity and open issues. Agents first.

delete.summary: Remove a Git connection and its links (admin)

get.summary: Development info of an issue
get.description: Branches, commits (latest five), pull requests and the latest build per pipeline that name the issue.

get.summary: Pull requests and builds of a release
get.description: Per issue of the version with Git activity: open and merged pull requests, failing builds.

get.summary: Liveness: the process is running
Readiness: the database is reachable
List imports
get.description: Requires the global permission `admin`.

post.summary: Import from Jira Server/DC
post.description:
Starts a job in the worker. With dryRun (the default) it reads everything and reports what it would create, map and skip, without writing. Project keys must be free in Lenipo. Objects imported before are skipped, so a second run adds only new ones. The token is kept only while the job runs.

Requires the global permission `admin`.

post.summary: Import a Confluence Server/DC space export
post.description:
The space XML export as a ZIP (field "file"). Pages with their versions, blog posts, comments, attachments and labels; Confluence macros become Lenipo macros where one exists. `spaceKey` names the new space (the export's key by default); dryRun (the default) only reports.

Requires the global permission `admin`.

post.summary: Import a project or space archive of another Lenipo
post.description:
The ZIP from "Export as archive" (field "file"). Everything gets new ids; people are matched by e-mail or created deactivated, issue types, statuses, priorities and link types by key or name. `targetKey` renames the project or space; dryRun (the default) only reports.

Requires the global permission `admin`.

post.summary: Import what a dry run checked
post.description:
Starts the real import with the file uploaded for the dry run (Confluence or archive).

Requires the global permission `admin`.

get.summary: Get an import with its progress, log and report
get.description: Requires the global permission `admin`.

get.summary: Export a project as archive
get.description:
Issues with comments, work logs, links, attachments, components and versions.

Requires the global permission `admin`.

get.summary: Export a space as archive
get.description:
Pages and blog posts with all versions, comments and attachments.

Requires the global permission `admin`.

post.summary: Change many issues at once
post.description: Edit, transition, move to a sprint, delete, watch or unwatch. Each issue goes through the same checks as a single change; the result lists which failed and why.

post.description: Each issue goes through the same checks as POST /issues. The result has one line per issue in the order sent. With "atomic": true they are created in one transaction: all or none.

post.description: Each change goes through the same checks as PATCH /issues/{key}. With "atomic": true all or none are made.

post.description: New keys, the old ones keep working. Type and status are kept where the target allows, else mapped (same category, else initial); components and versions by name; security level kept or the target default. Needs edit-issues in the source and create-issues in the target.

post.summary: Restore an issue from the trash
post.description: Brings back the subtasks deleted with it too. Needs delete-issues.
